phenotype_specificity.statement: Cohort-level only: the survey enrolled patients whose HA20 diagnosis was confirmed by functional analysis; TNFAIP3 was Sanger-sequenced or tested on an autoinflammatory gene panel. Results for other genes in this person are not reported. All four were initially diagnosed with Behçet's disease, the presentation the paper describes as characteristic of HA20.

quotes.quote: The diagnosis of HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of the TNFAIP3 variant.
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood for sequencing of all exons and exon-intron junctions of *TNFAIP3*.

Regarding recently identified cases, next-generation sequencing of target genes related to autoinflammatory disorders, including *TNFAIP3*, was performed at the Kazusa DNA Laboratory (Kisarazu, Japan).
Consequently, patients with HA20 present with autoinflammatory Behcet’s disease (BD)-like symptoms and may also develop autoimmune diseases (3).

segregation.statement: Four affected members of family F19 are each listed with c.805+1G>A. Their relationships are shown only in the pedigree figure (not interpretable from the text); unaffected relatives' genotypes are not stated. Cohort-level penetrance figure only.

Additionally, family analysis revealed that three cases with heterozygous variants were asymptomatic (penetrance: 95.7%).

functional.statement: Minigene splicing assay (construct: TNFAIP3 exons 3-8 in pCAGGS, in HEK293T; wild-type minigene as comparator): the c.805+1G>A minigene product showed skipping of exon 5 (c.635_805del; p.Asp212GlufsX). Patient RNA was not tested.

quotes.quote: Additionally, previously uncharacterized splice-site variants in *TNFIAP3* were functionally analyzed using the minigene splicing assay.
Three of these variants (c.487-1G\>A, c.805+1G\>A, and c.986+1G\>T) were introduced into WTex3-8, and the other (c.2088+1G\>A) into WTex7-9.
from the c.805+1G\>A minigene a skipping of exon 5 (c.635_805del; p.Asp212GlufsX) (**Supplementary Figure 4C**)

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Canonical splice-donor change at the exon 5 / intron 5 boundary (c.805+1G>A); predicted protein p.? in the batch. Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: heterozygous loss of function (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a hereditary autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in the TNFAIP3 gene (1).

authors_classification.statement: Cohort-level only: the authors describe all 35 distinct variants in the 54 surveyed patients with the words quoted. No per-variant ACMG criteria are stated.

quotes.quote: All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: protein_check differs: the paper's protein (pedigree p.Asn212GlufsX) reflects the minigene result (exon 5 skipping), not a cDNA prediction; the batch predicts p.?.
The paper contradicts itself on the residue: the pedigree figure writes p.Asn212GlufsX, the minigene results write p.Asp212GlufsX.
Exon 5 skipping is written as c.635_805del, which implies exon 5 starts at c.635; this was not checked against a transcript.
No case narratives and no prior report cited for family F19; no transcript named.
notes_for_panel: One family with four affected female carriers (Behçet-like disease) and a minigene showing exon 5 skipping.
